tags.name: Drops Endpoints
tags.description:
Endpoints for discovering drops, checking mint eligibility, building mint transactions, and creating drops.

Creating an ERC-721 SeaDrop V1 drop, in the usual order:

1. POST /api/v2/drops/deploy with drop_type `seadrop_v1_erc721`, send the transaction, then poll GET /api/v2/drops/deploy/{chain}/{tx_hash}/receipt for the collection slug.
2. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug} to save the stages, max supply, and payout address as a draft. Allowlists for `signed_presale` stages are uploaded first with POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/allowlist.
3. Items: POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/media for upload contexts and upload each file, optionally upload a metadata manifest with POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/manifest, then save them with POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/media/save-batch. Pass one upload_batch_id on every upload request for the set of files, then save that batch by filename.
4. Optionally, POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/prereveal-item to set the placeholder that every token shows until the reveal.
5. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/metadata/ipfs, polling GET /api/v2/drops/{slug}/metadata/ipfs/{workflow_execution_id} until it completes. This writes the real item metadata as the draft base URI.
6. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/publish, sending the transaction from the contract owner. The drop goes live once it is mined and indexed.
7. Minters use POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/mint.

Step 5 is the reveal. Run before the publish in step 6, the items are revealed as soon as the drop is live. To reveal later, publish without it, then run it and publish again when ready. POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/unpublish returns a transaction that closes a live drop.

An ERC-1155 self-mint drop (drop_type `seadrop_v2_erc1155_self_mint`) skips steps 2 to 7. After deploying, get a media_token for each item's file from POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/media and upload the file to the returned context. Each POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items with that token then returns a transaction that creates one token and mints its whole supply to the owner, and PUT /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/{token_id} returns one that updates an existing token's metadata.

put.description:
Changes an existing self-mint token's metadata and returns the ready-to-sign transaction that points the contract's base URI at the regenerated metadata. It does not change the token's supply. A token id that does not exist on the drop returns 404, and a drop that is not an ERC-1155 self-mint drop returns 400.

An ERC-1155 self-mint drop has no stages, publish step, or public mint. Each item is its own token id: saving one returns a transaction that creates it and mints its whole `supply` to the contract owner. The transaction's `to` is the drop's configurer contract (the one its getConfigurer() returns), not the drop contract, and it must be sent from `from`, the contract owner.

PATCH /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items/{token_id} takes the same body and saves the same metadata, but returns no transaction, so the contract keeps pointing at the old metadata. On a self-mint drop, use this endpoint and send its transaction.

get.description:
Get detailed drop information for a collection, including stages and supply.

`stages` is in the order the drop stores them, not sorted by start time. For a drop saved through POST /api/v2/drops/{slug} that puts the public stage first, although it runs last; sort by `start_time` for the schedule. A drop with no `public_sale` stage is allowlist only: only wallets on a presale allowlist can mint, and it ends when its last presale ends.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Collection slug

post.description:
Update an existing ERC-721 SeaDrop V1 drop and its stages. Only the collection owner can call it, and any other drop type returns 400.

Saves a Creator Studio draft. It does not change the live drop: SeaDrop stages are onchain contract state, so the draft has to be published separately before buyers see it. A 200 here means the draft was accepted, not that the drop changed.

`stages` replaces the whole set rather than merging, so send every stage the drop should end up with, including ones you are not changing. It is required even to change only `max_supply` or `creator_payout_address`. Reuse an existing stage uuid to update it, supply a new UUID to add one, and omit a stage to delete it. Every stage needs a `label`, and every price must be in the chain's native currency, with `price.contract_address` set to 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000.

A stage with a price above zero needs a creator payout address, the wallet that receives mint proceeds: SeaDrop reverts every paid mint while the contract has none. If the contract has no payout address yet, send `creator_payout_address` with the stages; a save with a paid stage and no payout address anywhere returns 400. Free stages need none.

Once minting has started, a save that raises `max_supply` or the price of the stage being minted from can be refused with 400. A drop whose supply or price is raised onchain during its mint is disabled.

The stage list has four rules, and rules 2 and 4 interact in a way worth reading before the first attempt:

1. At most one stage may be `public_sale`. A drop with none is allowlist only: only wallets on a presale allowlist can mint, and the drop ends when its last presale ends.
2. A public stage, when there is one, must be first in the array.
3. The presales, meaning every stage that is not `public_sale`, must be contiguous among themselves: each one starts exactly when the previous presale ended. The first presale start time is not constrained.
4. When there is a public stage, the last presale must end exactly when it starts.

Together, 2 and 4 mean array order is not chronological order: the public stage is listed first and runs last, with the presales running in array order before it. A drop with two allowlist stages therefore sends `[public, presale1, presale2]` while time runs presale1, then presale2, then public. Rule 3 does not tie presale1 back to the public stage, which is why the chain reads forward from presale1 rather than from the array head. An allowlist-only drop sends `[presale1, presale2]`, in time order.

Each stage's `max_total_mintable_by_wallet` is what that stage adds for a wallet, not a running total. Limits add up across the stages a wallet is listed on, a public stage adds its own limit on top, and mints a wallet leaves unused carry into later stages. So presales of 2 and 1 plus a public limit of 1 let a wallet on both lists mint 4.

A drop has at most 6 stages. An allowlist stage can also set `max_token_supply_for_stage`, a cap on the collection's total minted at which that stage stops, counting mints from every stage. A public stage cannot have one.

post.summary: Build publish transaction data for a drop
post.description:
Returns a ready-to-sign transaction that applies the drop's saved edits onchain: stages, supply, base URI, payout, and the OpenSea signer, fee recipient, and payers the drop needs. Every value is computed by OpenSea; do not build or change this calldata yourself, or signed presales stop validating.

Send the transaction from `from`, the contract's onchain owner. Only the collection owner can call this endpoint.

Only ERC-721 SeaDrop V1 drops are published. An ERC-1155 self-mint drop has no publish step and returns 400: each of its items goes onchain through the transaction POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/items returns.

A 400 carries the reason the drop cannot be published, for example that it is disabled, its launch date is still pending, it has no saved edits to apply, or a stage has a price while neither the saved edits nor the contract has a creator payout address (every paid mint would revert). After a first publish, the drop is live once GET /api/v2/drops/{slug} returns it, which happens after the transaction is mined and indexed.

To reveal, run POST /api/v2/drops/{slug}/metadata/ipfs, wait for it to complete, then call this endpoint again to put the new base URI onchain.

The transaction does not set a provenance hash or change contractURI(). SeaDrop only accepts setProvenanceHash() before the first token is minted, so a drop that wants one must send that call from the owner itself before minting starts; after the first mint it reverts.

post.summary: Build mint transaction data for a drop
post.description:
Returns ready-to-sign transaction data for minting tokens from a drop. The caller is responsible for signing and submitting the transaction. No wallet authentication is required, only an API key. The minter address in the request body determines who will receive the tokens. The transaction is built for the stage whose window contains the current time, and the response names it in `stage_uuid`, `stage_type`, `stage_start_time` and `stage_end_time`.

Supports ERC-721 SeaDrop V1 and ERC-1155 SeaDrop V2 drops. An ERC-1155 drop mints one token per request, named by `token_id`; an ERC-721 drop assigns token IDs onchain, so `token_id` must be omitted. Minting an ERC-1155 token while an allowlist (signed presale) stage is live on the drop, or from a paid stage priced in an ERC-20 token, is not yet supported and returns 400 with code UNSUPPORTED_DROP_TYPE.

Error bodies for the drop, stage and minter conditions below carry a stable `code` alongside `errors`. Branch on `code`, not on the message text.

A 422 means the drop is mintable but this mint is not: the minter is not on the active presale's allowlist (the message names the stage and, when the drop has a public stage, when it opens), the quantity is over the wallet's limit or the remaining supply (the message says how many remain), the minter cannot pay the price and gas, or the active stage has a price and the drop has no creator payout address, so every paid mint would revert until the creator sets one, or the active stage is paid and its OpenSea fee is below the drop's minimum, so OpenSea will not sign the mint until the creator publishes the stage again (STAGE_FEE_BELOW_FLOOR). GET /api/v2/drops/{slug} still shows such a stage as live.

post.summary: Exchange a scoped token for an access token
post.description:
Exchanges an opaque scoped token (personal access token) for a short-lived access token that satisfies `WalletAuth` on wallet-scoped endpoints. Send the returned `accessToken` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

This is the credential path for headless callers that hold no signing key: the scoped token in the request body is the only credential, so no session cookie, wallet signature, or API key is required. The alternative is the OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow described by the `WalletAuth` security scheme.

Failures are deliberately opaque. An unknown, revoked, rotated, or non-scoped subject token and a disabled integration all return the same 403 `Token exchange is not available`, so a 403 is not by itself evidence that the endpoint is unavailable. A 403 saying the access token could not be bound to the token's wallet means this scoped token cannot be exchanged again, usually because its wallet is no longer linked to the account: sign in again to create a new one instead of retrying.

400.description: Request body failed validation, for example a `subjectToken` outside the 10 to 8192 character range

403.description: Token exchange is not available. Returned for an unknown, revoked, or non-scoped subject token as well as for a disabled integration; the two are not distinguishable by design. Also returned, with its own message, when the access token cannot be bound to the subject token's wallet; retrying the same subject token does not help.

422.description: Body could not be read: malformed JSON, a missing required field, or an unsupported `subjectTokenType`

500.description: Exchange failed after the token was minted

For POST, add every fields entry unchanged as a multipart text field, then add a file part containing the bytes. The file part must be last. Let the HTTP library generate the multipart boundary; do not set the overall multipart Content-Type header yourself. POST storage uploads normally return 204. It is not reduced by what has already been minted or by the stage's supply cap. The public stage's own limit is added only on the public stage's result, not on any presale's. SeaDrop checks the cap against the wallet's lifetime minted count on the contract. For what the wallet can still mint, read mints_remaining.

It does not check the stage's time window, so an upcoming or ended stage still reports a number; compare start_time and end_time from GET /api/v2/drops/{slug}. 0 when the wallet or the stage has nothing left. Null when the wallet is not eligible for the stage, on ERC-1155 drops (limits there are per token), and when the wallet's onchain mint count could not be read.
